subject: Next steps: buying-path checkpoint & milestone plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya@edgehealth.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + MAP (draft) and procurement path ask

Thanks again for the quick call this morning — appreciate you both walking through the use case and procurement constraints. Short recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:  

Recap (3 bullets):
- Primary pilot scope: inference for anonymized clinical notes (low-to-medium throughput, bursty nightly batches).
- Key risk areas on your side: data handling controls and legal T&Cs (audit & indemnity language).
- Preferred outcome: production pilot behind EdgeHealth VPC or via Redwood Private for data residency.

Procurement path options (we discussed):
1) Card-first pilot: fastest (days) to get started; can be capped and instrumented.
2) PO + standard Redwood terms: typical commit path for production (requires signed order + PO issuance).
3) AWS Marketplace: neat for procurement but adds a channel setup step on both sides (we can support; varies by region).

Ask from you: which commercial path do you want prioritized (card / PO / marketplace)? Your selection will change milestone timings in the MAP.

Proposed mutual action plan (draft attached - EdgeHealth-MAP-v1.xlsx):
- Legal review (initial pass): 1 week for standard redline cycle; 2 weeks if vendor T&C escalation required.
- Security questionnaire + evidence (SOC2/creds): 1–3 weeks depending on requested scope; we can provide our SOC2 bundle and a security intake template to expedite.
- Finance & procurement review (PO vs card decision): 3–10 business days after legal signoff depending on internal PO cadence.
- PO issuance -> go-live: once PO is in, we can provision Dedicated/Private capacity in ~3 business days.

I'll attach the MAP draft and a short PO vs card cheatsheet (see attachments). If helpful I can also open a workspace in Google Drive and drop the security artifact bundle and a suggested SOW template.

Next steps I propose now:
- You tell us preferred commercial path (reply)
- We confirm legal point-people and share security artifact bundle (we'll drop in Drive link)
- Schedule a 30-min checkpoint next week to lock milestones (I suggested two times below)

Proposed checkpoint slots (pick one):
- Tue 2027-04-06 10:00am PT
- Wed 2027-04-07 02:00pm PT

Thanks — I'll stand up the MAP doc and add the proposed milestones once you confirm path.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + MAP (draft) and procurement path ask

Jonas — thanks for the recap and for putting the MAP together. A few quick clarifying questions before we pick a path:  

1) Marketplace: do you have an existing listing in AWS Marketplace (metered billing) or would that be a new onboarding flow? If it's already live, what is the expected lead time for our procurement/legal folks to approve that route?

2) Security artifacts: would you be able to share your SOC2 Type II report and also a short intake checklist we can give to our InfoSec? That will speed the security review.

3) Legal timing: what is Redwood's typical turnaround on contract redlines for a standard SOW? Are there any non-negotiable clauses we should be aware of in advance?

4) Finance: if we go card-first for pilot, what constraints are there on token usage and can you set hard caps?

We'd like to move quickly but need to align internally (legal + security + finance). From our side I can commit to lining up procurement and will follow up with an internal preferred path by EOD Mon 2027-04-05.

Thanks,
Priya Rao
Head of Procurement, EdgeHealth
priya@edgehealth.com

Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + MAP (draft) and procurement path ask

Thanks Priya — quick answers inline and an updated suggested timeline below.

1) Marketplace: Redwood currently supports an AWS Marketplace listing for our hosted API and selected packaging for Dedicated (we do onboard customers there). Marketplace listing can shorten procurement approval for some companies but requires seller onboarding and billing configuration. For EdgeHealth I expect marketplace onboarding to add ~2–3 weeks upfront versus card-first. If procurement prefers speed, card-first -> convert to marketplace for production is common.

2) Security artifacts: attaching our SOC2 bundle and a one-page security intake checklist to this thread (I dropped the full bundle to the Drive folder linked in the MAP). That should cover InfoSec's initial evidence requests.

3) Legal timing: for a standard SOW most cycles are 1 week (initial redline) + 3–7 business days for final sign if only minor edits. If EdgeHealth legal insists on any indemnity/limitation changes we should expect an additional round. The attached doc TnC-redlines-edgehealth.pdf shows the handful of clauses customers frequently flag.

4) Card-first constraints: yes, we can put hard usage caps on the account and set daily token limits; we'll also set up alerting to prevent surprise spend. Card is the fastest path to get a pilot live (typically <3 business days).

Updated suggested MAP milestones (feel free to edit in the attached XLSX):
- Day 0: kickoff + MAP acceptance (we agree path: card / PO / marketplace)
- Days 1–7: legal first-pass + security intake (SOC2 bundle shared)
- Days 8–21: security deep-dive & evidence exchange (if requested)
- Post-legal signoff: finance issues PO (3–10 business days) OR we enable card pilot immediately
- After PO/card: provisioning (3 business days) -> pilot start

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min checkpoint on Tue 2027-04-06 10:00am PT to finalize path and owners. I'll also add the T&C redlines file to the Drive folder and create a HubSpot task for legal follow-up (link below).

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890
Drive MAP folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_MAP

Attaching: TnC-redlines-edgehealth.pdf (short), SOC2-bundle.zip (link in Drive)

Best,
Jonas
